utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Do you have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, my name is Niemann. I appear with my colleagues, Mr. Turone, Ms. McHenry and Mr. Huber for the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Edina Residovic, representing here today, Mr. Zejnil Delalic, together with my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan Professor of Law from Canada. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name Zeljko Olujic. I am defending here Mr. Zdravko Mucic, together with my colleague, Mr. Tomislav Kuzmanovic, who is absent this morning and will not join us in the courtroom today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, I representing Mr. Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, I am Cynthia McMurrey, along with my colleague, Ms. Nancy Boler. We represent Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we're still on with Ms. Residovic. May we have your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour, I will call the witness immediately. This morning we have provided the court with the list of witnesses and the possibilities of the -- the opportunities of the defence to call them and have them examined, so I would appreciate if you can tell us your opinion on our proposal regarding the witness list today. Thank you. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose this is in addition to the witnesses you've already called?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't hear what you said because I didn't have my earphones on. I didn't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I was commenting these latest witness list is in addition to witnesses already called?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a continuation beginning with today and these are only witnesses who have been already put on the list, but we have reduced the number. We have left out eight witnesses, so this would be our final proposal and this would conclude the case of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: As long as the difficulties likely to be imposed by duplication and repetition, there's nothing wrong in your witness list, as long as we don't have duplication or repetition of evidence. I would like you to call them, please. Because what we said from the beginning is that evidence which is obviously relevant because they are duplicated or repetitive, then the evidence could be called. We will go on. They are your witnesses, you know how to examine them and what you'll have to say to avoid those principles. Thank you, you can carry on. Swear the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: EXAMINATION-IN-CHIEF BY MS. RESIDOVIC:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please state your full name and introduce yourself to this chamber?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Mustafa Dzelilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, before I proceed with my questions to you during this examination-in-chief, I have to draw your attention to a technical matter. You and I speak the same language and it would be very easy for you to answer immediately each of my questions. However, our conversation has to be interpreted so that the Honourable Judges and all other participants in the proceedings here in the courtroom can understand us. Therefore, I kindly ask you, when I ask my question, to wait for the interpretation coming from the earphones on your table. So after the interpretation is completed, you can answer my question. Mr. Dzelilovic, have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dzelilovic, could you tell me where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in Hadzici on the 13th of November, 1955.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background and what is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: My ethnic background is Bosniak and I am a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your occupation, Mr. Dzelilovic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I am an ergonomist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your educational background, where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary education in Hadzici and secondary school in Sarajevo and I graduated from the faculty of ergonomy in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, could you tell us now where were you in 1992 when the war started in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The aggression on Bosnia-Herzegovina found me in Hadzici, where I was president of the Municipality of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, the Court knows quite a bit about Bosnia and Herzegovina and the area in question, but still, I would like you to tell us whether the Municipality of Hadzici belonged to the area of Sarajevo town?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The Municipality of Hadzici was part of Sarajevo. It was one of the ten municipalities that made up the Town of Sarajevo, the City of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question to clarify this issue, so that we know exactly which area we are talking about. Could you tell us where exactly this municipality is located, in which direction from the Town of Sarajevo and where precisely it is located?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The Municipality of Hadizi is situated on the road Number M-17. On the south it borders the Municipality of Konjic and on the west, the municipalities of Kresevo and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, at this moment, we would be interested in the southern part of your municipality, could you tell us with which villages belonging to the Konjic Municipality your Municipality of Hadzici borders?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The border is near the Evan Sedlo Ridge. And it's situated near the village of Bradina, which belongs to the Municipality of Konjic. On our side, there are villages of Vranske Stijene and Janici. And there's a tunnel going under the Ivan Planina mountain. And this is sort of bordered between these two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, so far the court has heard the names of Hadizi and Pazaric and Tarcin. However, could you tell us where in relation to your municipality where these villages are situated?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: There are eleven local communes in the village of Hadizi and there are three residential urban areas Hadizi, Pazaric and Tarcin. The remaining local communes are villages, that is rural areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, you just said that your municipality, together with these residential areas is located on a strategically important road, M-17, could you now tell us whether there were any other reasons why your municipality had military and strategic significance at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was an important strategic point at the time because of a number of military installations on the territory of the municipality. The municipality comprised one part of the Bjela Sjzni (phoen) mountain, which from a strategically point of view is a very important area. And a technological -- a military technological institute was located in Hadzici, where military equipment was repaired and there was a very important warehouse where weapons were stored in the area. The place is called Zunovica. And there is another military depot in the area and the barracks in Pazaric. And at Usivak there was a barracks, whose main function was communication at the time. Therefore, we can talk about a very important municipality from the strategical point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, such a geographical location in the installations belonging to the former JNA that you have just mentioned, were they the reason of the -- for the attitude of the former JNA towards this particular municipality? The attitude and behaviour of the JNA. Again, I am reminding you that this is a municipality which was part of the Town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the former JNA thought the area was quite important and it wanted to capture it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the President of Municipality and later on as the President of the war Presidency of the Municipality of Hadizi, do you know whether the former JNA managed to fulfil their objective and when?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. After the events that took place in Sarajevo, in the month of April, the Yugoslav Peoples Army, together with the SDS forces, set up a blockade on the M-17 road and captured a junction leading to Kiseljak in Hadzici, which was strategically very important because it was coming from the direction of Sarajevo. On the other hand, the former JNA armed the para military formations of the SDS in the area of Ivan Planina Mountain. Therefore, there was evidence, reliable evidence, that they were fulfilling their plan. They were implementing their aggressive policy and they were very open about it throughout the month of April. They were acting in support of the pro Chetnik SDS forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, the former JNA, did it operate, in a military sense, in the territory of the Hadzici municipality and what happened at that time with the authorities, with the local authorities and the population of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, on 9th of May, the former Yugoslav Peoples Army carried out an aggression against our municipality with tanks, rocket launchers, APCs, anti-aircraft weapons. It attacked the Town of Hadzici. And pushed away the police forces that were trying to put up some sort of resistance, but to no avail because at that time the police had a very small amount of infantry weapons at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Is it necessary to go into all those details? Why don't you come straight away to the point?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that these data are quite important when it comes to the assignments of the tactical group and the possible responsibility of its commanders in their area of responsibility. This municipality is part of the Town of Sarajevo and we thought that this person who is a fact witness, can describe the situation in which Mr. Delalic found himself for about half a year. I think that without the description of these circumstances, it is difficult to understand his responsibilities and his task he was commander of the tactical group. These are the only reasons actually. I mean, we're simply not trying to talk about the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I didn't know these possibilities are in dispute. We're not in dispute, commander of TG-1, that he has responsibilities, nobody disputes that. What brings all the charges, are the exercise of his authority as TG-1 commander, not that he has authority as TG-1 commander, not his responsibility, that is not in dispute. Nobody disputes that. The Prosecutor is here. We know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but it is the Prosecutor's case that he, as the commander of all formations was responsible for everything, including Celebici. If he's not responsible for anything, then how can he be responsible for Celebici. This is our response. We are bringing here, people who were in the area at the time. Who can testify from their personal knowledge about something that I as a lawyer could couldn't tell you. And this is the reason why we call these people from Jablanica, Prozor, Hadzici, and Konjic. We are trying to provide you with an opportunity to see what kind of responsibilities he had. And it's probably after their evidence that you will be able to reach a decision about his responsibilities, whether the Prosecution is right or the defence, because, again, we cannot present you with any proof regarding, for example, hangar 6 because my client was not there. And we do not have fact witnesses who will testify to that. So we are trying to focus on a wider area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's not an issue, -- and explain, and my brother has also the details of what happened has nothing to do with whether he exercised his responsibilities properly. This is what he's staying. It has nothing to do with that. Because while he was appointed, why Hadzici was unsafe and what JNA did, has nothing to do with his exercise of his responsibility. Because what brings him into the offence is his exercise of responsibility. And his role towards that. As I have already said, perhaps it's your own understanding of what the charge is, but it's very clear. And what this witness has set out to tell us is, the role and responsibility of Delalic as TG-1 commander. And particularly from the 1st of May to October. All these are the background information, has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence believes that this is important, so, of course, you can always say that the question is not relevant, but we believe that the reasons, that is the assignments that were carried out by Delalic's commander, tactical group 1 we believe that this is important. I will try not to burden this court with all the superfluous details, because the details which are not important for the defence of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Following the instructions of the chamber, Mr. Dzelilovic, I will simply ask you then, where did the local authorities withdraw after the former JNA and the SDS took over the centre of the town the way you described?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The local authorities withdrew to Pasaric together with the population that managed to pull out from Hadzici. Unfortunately, 186 people remained there forever and we don't know what happened to them to this date. Therefore, the seat of the Hadzici municipality from the beginning of the war until the signing of the Dayton accord was in Pasaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to my previous question, Mr. Dzelilovic, you said that your municipality was bordering the Municipality of Konjic in the area of Ivan Planina Mountain and that this area was blocked as early as April, what did this blockade of the road to Konjic mean for the population of the village of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The population of the Hadzici municipality found themselves stuck between the area of Konjic and the area of Hadzici, we did not have any way out from our municipality except through Vlakiseljac (phoen), so what this meant for the local population was that, for example, the wounded and the sick had to be transported to the first medical institution along the road for about 15 or 16 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would you normally travel from Pasaric to Konjic? And how did that trip change after the blockade?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that trip used to last less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We have already been told about that by Dokramovic, Mr. Dzelilovic. We have also been told by General Divjak if you don't have access through Mount Ivan, then you have to travel about 16 passes, what is the necessity of that? Ask us about TG-1, tactical group, then we will know what responsibilities are. Why go into unnecessary details?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will follow your instructions, however, after the testimony of General Divjak the Prosecution did not change their allegations and are claiming that these forces attacked peaceful Serb villages, and that's why we're trying through these witnesses who lived at the time in the area to describe the situation. This may be beyond dispute for you but as long as the charges are as they stand, we have an obligation to question these witnesses to that effect. I know that you have been convinced of that, but it is still the Prosecutor's case that the situation was such. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I have not been convinced, but please go ahead with your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said that you only needed half an hour to go there, and after the siege?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we needed 15 or 16 hours along a dirt road to reach the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I said -- I said "I am not sure." I said, "I am not sure that I have been convinced." Not that I have not been convinced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The population of Hadzici, which at the time was reduced to that restricted area, did they -- was the lifting of the blockade of vital significance for them at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a question of life and death for the population of Hadzici, was the only way out, and such an operation had to take place. At that time there was a great number of refugees in the area who had come from Eastern Bosnia with the horrible stories about killings and rapes, and we are talking about a very restricted area, 200 square kilometres, the area which was constantly exposed to shelling and air attacks. So we didn't have adequate medical protection. And as I say, it was a question of life and death. It was something that had to be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, I believe that we have described the general situation in the area at the time, and right now I would like to move to another area. Mr. Dzelilovic, could you tell me whether you knew Mr. Zejnil Delalic before the war and if you had an opportunity to meet with him between April and November 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know Zejnil Delalic before the war, and the first time I met with him was in April in Konjic, when together, with the representatives of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Hadzici, and representatives of the police, when I managed to reach Konjic via this dirt road that I mentioned. And this is when I first met Zejnil Delalic. At that time he was involved with logistics and he helped us on that occasion with some supplies. He gave us some uniforms, Motorola’s, medical supplies and so on. That was our first meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that meeting in April, did you at any point in time come across Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Our next meeting took place in mid-May, I'm not sure, maybe a little later. It was after we had received information that Zejnil Delalic was in Zagreb and that he was supposed to obtain some technical supplies. And we were told that a convoy was supposed to pass through Dusina on the way to Visoko. So together with the representatives of the representatives of the municipal staff and the police, I went to Ducina, and this is where I met with him the second time. Part of the supplies were given to the Municipality of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met with Mr. Zejnil Delalic in Ducina in this second half of May, what function did he perform at the time, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think he was in charge of escorting the convoy, because he had been in Zagreb, he was supposed to obtain these supplies, so he came with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time was there anyone else, besides members of the municipal staff, was there anyone else in Ducina and did anyone else take over the supplies that had been obtained in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, Mr. Mustafa Polutak was also there, and he was representing the Tactical Group that had been established some time before that. So I think that he took over a certain amount of weapons for the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, in view of your knowledge about the meeting in Ducina, could you tell us whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic, at that time, was a civilian, as far as you knew, or did he have some other function? When you first met Mr. Zejnil Delalic, did you see him as a civilian, and what was the situation in that regard during your second meeting with him?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a civilian all the time until he was appointed as the commander of the Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, after the month of May, have you met Mr. Delalic, and what tasks and functions did he hold at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I met Zejnil Delalic at the area of Hadzici, when we conducted an electrification introduction of electrical current into our villages of the municipality, because the electrical current supply was interrupted from Hadzici. So we had took certain measures to repair the supply network. And in cooperation with Zejnil Delalic, we managed to do so from the direction of Konjic. We also met again, due to reconstruction of the railroad, repairs to the railroad, between Hadzici and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now move onto another topic, after we have gone thoroughly through your knowledge of Zejnil Delalic's functions between April and June. Would you please tell me whether your troops took part in some of combat operations, together with the units of Konjic, within that period that we have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had a joint operation to deblock road M17 around Bradina. On our part we had the Territorial Defence of Hadzici units and the unit of the public safety of our municipality, meaning the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your side, who commanded the Territorial Defence units which took part in the deblocking of the road, and who was in charge of the police units?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence units were commanded by their commander, a commander of the local headquarters, Territorial Defence. Police had its own hierarchy and subordination. They had the head of the police at the station or precinct of public security in Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your knowledge, would you know who was in charge of the units on the other side of Ivan Planina, meaning from the direction of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, could you claim that the units which were in action from -- on your part, were commanded by the people that you have stated? Were there some third parties or other persons from other municipalities who, at that time, could have attained any command or responsibility over the units of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I state that the command of our units was done solely by the commander of our municipal staff and the head of the police and the public security of Hadzici, and the command for that attack was given by the Territorial Defence headquarters of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long, if you could remember, did that operation of deblocking of Bradina -- how long did it last, at least when it concerns your units?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Operations were concluded within two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if those forces of armed Serb population, did they resist?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, their resistance was fierce. Within the first day we had 14 wounded. Our units have moved on somewhat earlier, and Chetnik forces in Bradina probably thought that the attack is coming only from our direction, and they resisted. They resisted severely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, at any point in the area of your municipality was there a commander at the headquarters or commanding staff of the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the Tactical Group, as I have said, was Polutak Mustafa, Lieutenant-Colonel of the former JNA. He came to Pazaric and -- and a seat of the Tactical Group 1 from that moment on was in Pazaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when Mr. Polutak was the commander of Tactical Group 1, do you know whether certain units of the municipal Territorial Defence were under the command of Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A part of our units was. A certain number of people, around 300, was under the command of the Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since all the combat operations were conducted in the area of your municipality, would you tell me, at that time did you know or do you know that in some of the operations of Tactical Group 1 the units of Konjic also took part?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. As part of Tactical Group 1, there were also units from Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, and when those units arrived from those areas, they were well equipped, and it was then said that the equipping of those units was performed by Mr. Delalic, which was, for our current conditions, a big thing. Because we had -- we tried daily to try to reject the forces, the attacks, which were attacking us on a daily basis from all directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, I will now ask you a question concerning the combat operation, because we have another witness, we have here, Lieutenant-Colonel Polutak, but I would like to ask you, since you were a direct witness, do you know whether in that operation, when the commander was Mr. Polutak, did Zejnil Delalic command, have command of the units coming from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Those units were subordinated to Tactical Group 1, as well as parts of the municipal Territorial Defence were subordinated to Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you again to talk on another topic, because I believe we have obtained enough facts to the Chamber about your knowledge of Tactical Group 1, while it was under command of Mr. Polutak. Mr. Dzelilovic, you have said that at the beginning of the war you were the head of the Municipal Assembly. Can you tell me, until when in 1992 did you stay -- did you hold that function; and in your municipality, when you were unable to conduct meetings of the assembly, did you have any other local authority body operational?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: During the entire time of the war, I held my position. At the periods when we were unable to hold meetings, we had a functioning Presidency of the Hadzici municipality, and this is a term -- a war term of so-called war Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mean this was not a part of the law, of the legislation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The Presidency was functioning because we had the sufficient number of representatives to occasionally hold meetings of the assembly, to verify the decisions that we as members of the Presidency made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Municipal Assembly, or your war Presidency, when there was a lack of possibility to hold meetings of the Assembly, did you have the authority to name to post commanders of the units within your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. The war Presidency did not have a competence to appoint commanders. We could give suggestions, but the appointment was done by the regional Territorial Defence headquarters, or the headquarters of Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your Municipality of Hadzici, did -- commanders of the municipal headquarters were members of your war Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the Presidency, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember, Mr. Dzelilovic, whether that period between April and October, who were the commanders of the municipal headquarters, Territorial Defence in Hadzici, or did you just have one commander?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: When the aggression on the Municipality of Hadzici began, the commander was Ramiz Stupovac. He was appointed earlier, while there was still not a war going on. After that we had Said Rizvic, after whom Camur, after which Kazic and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, since there were operations at that moment, whether some of the people -- some of the commanders were wounded or they were killed, but was it usual to appoint in such cases new commanders on the part of the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because there was a very serious front line. We had daily attacks and we had wounded and killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. Dzelilovic, whether the head of the police precinct was a member of your war Presidency, and whether he was his subordinate?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The head of the public security was a member of the presidency, as well as the Secretary of Territorial -- of the Peoples Defence, but the Presidency did not have a superior authority over the head of the police precinct of the police. They have their CSV subordination, this is the Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question relating to the topic. Could you tell me, Mr. Dzelilovic, who were the forces of defence in Hadzici within that period?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Those were Territorial Defence and the units of public security of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already answered that since Mr. Polutak came, from then on the seat of Tactical Group 1 was in the area of your municipality. Can you, as the head of municipality, although this data may be more familiar to the commander or Territorial Defence, but could you tell us how many soldiers of your municipality were subordinated to the commander of Tactical Group 1 during certain combat operations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You said 300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That's the number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Honourable Chamber, I may have heard it incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose subordination were the remaining units of your municipality, those who were not subordinated to the commander of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Those units were under the command of the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, tell me how long would such combat operations take, how much time would they take, the operations conducted by the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Between seven and ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any periods you had a more extensive operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In August or November we had the operation JUG or south '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know what happened to soldiers who were subordinated to the commander of Tactical Group 1 after such operations would cease?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Those units would then be returned to the Territorial Defence at the municipal headquarters, and then at those periods they were under the command of the Territorial Defence headquarters. They would return to their basic unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, within a period of time in the area of your municipality was there another seat or a newly formed Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Tactical Group 2 was founded with a seat in Igman in the Hotel Borik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know if a part of units of your Hadzici municipality was subordinated also to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A part of our units of Territorial Defence of Hadzici municipality was subordinated to Tactical Group 1, and another part was subordinated to Tactical Group 2. A part of units remained at the front line under the command of the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know whether either of the tactical groups, number 1 or number 2, which was founded later, was in command over the Territorial Defence headquarters of Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were never in command to our municipal headquarters. It was in command only to some units which were, at given moments, part of Tactical Group 1 or 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, in accordance to your knowledge of the situation in the municipality, has either of the tactical groups, Tactical Group 1 or 2, did they have command or authority over certain institutions of the area of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Tactical Groups 1 and 2 did not have authority over any institutions excepting the units which were subordinated, the TO, the Territorial Defence units, subordinated to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe we are clear enough, but nevertheless I will ask you to respond to a more precise question, whether Tactical Group 1 or Tactical Group 2, did they have control of a prison facility or did they have authority over a prison facility which potentially existed at the territory of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Tactical Group 1, Tactical Group 2 did not have any authority, any competence concerning prison facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, could we now move onto yet another topic, which would be of interest to us. If you can respond to questions posed to you. In your knowledge, Mr. Dzelilovic, did Mr. Zejnil Delalic in 1992, was he named or appointed as a commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After an accident that Mr. Polutak had, when the place was -- the post was vacant, then the commander of Tactical Group 1 became Zejnil Delalic. It seems to me it was in July or August, beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you met him right away when he came to Pazaric, i.e. the area of your municipality, and can you remember who was with him at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I met him, I went to congratulate him, and he had with him the head of the Territorial Defence, commander Sucho Paritza (phoen). I congratulated him, I wished him all the best, because the war on the front line in my municipality was a very hard one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, from that moment when Mr. Delalic, as you say, at the end of July or beginning of August, when he was appointed as a commander of Tactical Group 1, from that moment on did he become a superior authority over the Municipal Assembly, the war Presidency, or personally yourself?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never had anybody as my superior authority, any commander. He was only in command of the units or parts of the units of our Territorial Defence which became part of Tactical Group 1. The principle is the same as it was when Mr. Polutak was in charge, so he does not have a superior authority over war Presidency of our municipality. This is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, from the moment of his appearance when he came, did he become the superior authority to the Territorial Defence headquarters of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I have already said that. He is only in command of those parts of units which were transferred from the Territorial Defence of Hadzici and put under the command of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if within that period a certain number of units was subordinated to Mr. Delalic as the commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether a part of units from the Municipality of Hadzici was subordinated to Tactical Group 1 at the time of -- when Mr. Zejnil Delalic was commander?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was in command -- those units were subordinated to Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2, that is a part of units of our Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know who was the commander of Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Commander of Tactical Group 2 was Mirsad Catic and after he had been wounded, this function was taken over by the chief of staff, a Mr. Huso Alic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know under whose authority were the prisons in the area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The prisons were under the authority of the public security stations in my municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you stated, Mr. Dzelilovic, that the formations of the armed forces in your municipality were composed of the MUP units and Territorial Defence units, could you tell me whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic was ever commander of all the formations in the area? That is, the MUP units, the Territorial Defence units in the territory of your municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. He was only the commander of the units who were subordinated to Tactical Group 1. I believe that this is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, at that time, in 1992, in the territory of the Hadzici municipality, did any judicial bodies function? That is, Courts' and Prosecutor's offices.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, Prosecutor's offices did not exist at the time in Hadzici. We belong to the judicial area of Sarajevo. That is, our municipality is within the competence of the Sarajevo courts. We only had a magistrate court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The court already knows that the magistrate's court is an administrative type of court. And right now I would like to ask you something else, Mr. Dzelilovic. As the President of the municipality, did you have authority to establish a court or public Prosecutor's office on the territory of your municipality and did you have authority to appoint judges?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not. This is not within the authority of the municipality. This is within the competence of the ministry of justice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's one other topic that I would like to discuss with you, Mr. Dzelilovic, do you know where Celebici is located?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Celebici is located on the M-17 road in the direction of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, in 1992, did you know that there was a barracks there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew even before the war that there used to be a military barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, did you ever visit the barracks in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, Mr. Dzelilovic, were you aware that there was a prison situated within that barracks?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, in 1992, or at any other point later on, did you learn that Tactical Group 1 or its commander, Zejnil Delalic, had any authority over that prison?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, this can't be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How can he say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I didn't hear that there was any prison there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: In any case, how can he say that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, several very brief questions regarding one particular issue. Mr. Dzelilovic, you said that the western side, your municipality borders with Kiseljak. Could you tell me whether in 1992, on the territory of your municipality, whether there were any problems with the HVO forces, although, at the beginning, the HVO forces and the forces of BiH army acted together?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: On the territory of the Hadzici municipality there were no HVO forces. However, we had to use the road via Kresevo and Kiseljak and we encountered a number of problems when we wanted to pass through that area. Conveys were looted and people were arrested and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was arrested by the HVO on nine occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that at the time these forces conducted propaganda against a certain number of people?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware about this propaganda. It was constant. The object was to discredit the politicians in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was a campaign conducted by the media and it lasted throughout the war. I guess this is the usual thing that happens in any war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one last question, Mr. Dzelilovic, considering the fact that the seat of commanders of Tactical Groups 1 and 2 were in your area, do you have any personal knowledge that in that time, there was a very severe campaign that was being conducted against the commanders, Delalic and Catic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know that that propaganda was master-minded in order to endanger the morale of the members of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, in spite of all these efforts to lift the blockade of the town, how long did these military activities last in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, military operations lasted throughout the war. But when it comes to this period, the period of very intense fighting, the operations lasted throughout July, August and September. Unfortunately, we were not successful. And we did not manage to help the local population out and to lift the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dzelilovic, this concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Defence of Mr. Mucic has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Hazim Delic has no questions for this witness either. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Esad Landzo has no questions for this witness either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Questions for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, we have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzelilovic, my name is Turone and I will ask you some questions for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, you told the court already about the strategic importance of your municipality, Hadzici. Do you agree with me that Hadzici had a particularly significant importance for the purpose of lifting the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did from the strategic point of view. On the right side of the Hadzici municipality, there's the Mount Igman. And on the other side, to the south, there's the Mount Ivan. So these are two very important strategic points in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you have admitted that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You answered it yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That's enough for me, Mr. Dzelilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that for this reason, Hadzici was chosen one of the two lines of attack in order to lift the siege of Sarajevo? Is that correct? The other line of attack being Visoko, you're aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I know about Visoko, yes, but I can only be a fact witness for the events that took place in my area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Yeah, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: But I understand why there were attempts made in that area because this was very close to our municipality, maybe only 2 or 3 kilometres away. And this is all we needed to lift the blockade of Sarajevo. And that is why this particular location was chosen for lifting the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's talk not about the line of attack of Visiko, but the line of attack of Hadzici, which concerned your municipality. Do you agree with me that the line of attack of Hadzici was the one entrusted to Tactical Group 1, is that okay? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And are you aware, by the way, that the other line of attack, the one of Visoko was entrusted to Tactical Group 2?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right. That's enough for me. Thank you. Just about Tactical Group 2, you named some commanders of them. Are you aware that another commander of Tactical Group 2, some time at the beginning was Colonel Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You mean you're not aware?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think he was. I know that Mirsad Catic was commander of Tactical Group 2. I know that, but I don't know about Rasim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In any case, do you know this person, Rasim Delic, Colonel Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. He's the commander in chief of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And what about his capacity in May, was he already commander in chief in May, '92?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And what was his capacity in May, '92, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what he did in May, I know that at that time, the commander was Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see, you've within saying something to the court about the Bradina blockade, et cetera, and about the roundabout routes that were necessary to reach Konjic from Pasaric, do you agree with me that before the blockade was eliminated you had to follow these roundabout routes to reach Konjic, passing through Fojnica and Dusina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose that's what he said in a roundabout way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Actually, he didn't say exactly through which villages or town did this roundabout route pass. I would like to know whether these roundabout routes would pass through Fojnica and Dusina?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes, they went through the municipalities of Kresevo, Kiseljak and then the Municipality of Fojnica and then all the way down to Konjic. But we're talking about dirt roads and very small roads going through the woods. If you have a map, I could easily point it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said Dusina was on this roundabout and that because of the M-17 blockade. Do you agree with me that the attack on Bradina on May 25 was carried on precisely in order to eliminate the blockade on the main road, M-17, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: That was the basic objective of the operation, to lift the blockade of the M-17 road and to prevent the Chetnik units from joining with each other, the Chetnik units from Bradina and surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And let's go now to that day of about mid-May, '92, when you met with Zejnil Delalic in Dusina. That was, of course, before the blockade was eliminated, is that correct? In mid-May, yes, certainly so. Do you agree with me that in that occasion, that day, you had a meeting in Dusina, not only with Delalic and Polutak, but also with Rasim Delic, Dinko Sebic and Hasan Cengic that day in Dusina, did you see these people in Dusina that day?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I only saw Dinko Zebic, Polutak and some other people who were escorting the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you don't remember having seen Rasim Delic and Hasan Cengic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about Dinko Zebic, what was Dinko Zebic doing there that day?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was just introduced to him on that occasion by someone, but I don't know what he was doing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But, on this occasion, when you met these people in Dusina; Delalic, Polutak, Dinko Zebic, do you agree with me that you had some discussion about the need for breaking the Bradina blockade, which was still on, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't discuss anything with Dinko Zebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I mean with any of the other people, you were in Dusina on that roundabout route because of the blockade of M-17 road, is this your testimony, that meeting with these people that day in Dusina, you didn't talk about the Bradina blockade at all?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, the only reason why I was there was to take over part of the technical supplies. That was the only thing I was interested in at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But, isn't that true that during this meeting with these people in Dusina, also the formation of Tactical Groups, 1 and 2, was discussed somehow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He told you he went there to take over his supplies. That's all why he was there. That's what he has just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: All right, Your Honours. I will pass on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since a detention camp for Serb prisoners existed in your municipality as well, is that correct, that a Serb detention unit was in the silos of Tarcin in '92?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It was not a camp, it was a prison. And it is true that it was located in Tarcin. And it's a prison, not a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: That's okay, a prison is all right. And then focusing for a moment on this detention unit, this prison in Tarcin, is that correct that the commander of the Tarcin camp in ‘92 was Becir Hujic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, what's the relevance of these questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This issue has been touched by Ms. Residovic in examination-in-chief, probably just to try to show how prisons were regulated in a similar way in different municipalities. That is why I think we are entitled to go through that issue too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In that case, you might limit your questions to that of Catic because he's says he's never had authority over any prisons in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am talking about the Tarcin prison. I'm sorry, this Becir Hujic was a commander, whose unit did Becir Hujic belong to?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, as far as the prison in Tarcin is concerned, it was under the competence of the public security stations in Hadzici, that is the local MUP. Because at that time, the Territorial Defence could not have established a prison according to the then regulations. That is, the captured sniper shooters and prisoners of war were surrendered to the public security station in Hadzici and they were in charge of subsequent proceedings. And I, myself, was never present in that prison, nor was I interested in it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But, do you agree with me that in any case, in 1992, the Tarcin prison was under the supervision, the superior control of the 109th mountain brigade of the Bosnia army led by Nezir Kazic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, in 1992, the prison was under the control of the public security station. Only after the indictments were issued, the military, whatever concerned military jurisdiction, it was only then that it was placed under the control of the 109th mountain brigade. Because the cases dealt with war prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Tried by a military court. After indictment, the cases are tried by the military court or the civil courts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure the police was in charge of the proceedings and they submitted criminal reports. I don't know who tried these cases. I know that judges were coming, but it was only in 1994 that they proceeded with trials, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Is that possible to ask for a break and have, eventually, one or more questions after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you're exhausted, then you don't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In this case, my cross-examination is finished, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is the end of the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you don't have any questions, you don't have to invent any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honour. RE-EXAMINED BY MS. RESIDOVIC:

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzelilovic, during the cross-examination, you stated the Catic was commander of Tactical Group 2, this is what you stated during your examination-in-chief as well. Could you just tell us in which area of your municipality did this particular Tactical Group operate?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It operated in the area of the Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: This tactical group, did it ever operate from the area of Visoko?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Very invigorating about whether Catic was commander of Tactical Group 2. That's all that was asked. It was suggested that it was him. It was then asserted, so I don't see why there should be an ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was not clear in what direction it was. Because the witness has just told us that the it was located in Mount Igman and before it was claimed that it was in some other area, and I was just trying to clarify this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I did not even bother about locations, I just wanted to know whether Catic or some other person was commander of the TG-2. You are now expanding it into the jurisdiction of...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, from the transcript you will see that Visoko was mentioned and this concludes my examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Dzelilovic, thank you. This is all for you and you are discharged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble at twelve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, your next witness. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Swear the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may sit down. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SABAN DURACIC EXAMINED BY MS. RESIDOVIC:

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Will you please introduce yourself to the court by stating your full first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Saban Duracic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, before I ask questions of you with respect to your knowledge of the events of 1992, I would like to draw your attention to a technical point. You and I both speak the same language; you would be able to very quickly respond to my questions. However, the interpreters need to interpret every question and every answer to one of the working languages of the Tribunal, so that the Trial Chamber and everyone else in the court would be able to follow our conversation. So I will ask you to please wait for my question to be interpreted, and you will hear the sound coming from a set that is on your desk to your left, and only then answer the question. In this way, everybody will be able to follow and we will avoid any confusion during this examination. Mr. Duracic, did you understand the instructions that I just gave you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Duracic, would you please tell us when and where you were born?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on 18 August 1941 in the village of Koto in the Municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background and citizenship?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak Muslim and I am a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, where do you live?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is your profession, please?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I am a construction technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what has your formal training been?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I completed secondary technical school in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, where did you work before the outbreak of war in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Until the outbreak of war, I worked in the public utility company, water -- for water and sewage, as a leader in the technical department.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, where were you at the outbreak of war in April -- on April 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I was at work at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Duracic, when you joined the defence forces of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after the first shelling of Sarajevo, I joined the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What were your initial tasks after you reported to the Territorial Defence and were mobilised into the defence of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Since I am an officer engineer, my first task was to provide security, in terms of engineering of the facility where the war Presidency was to be located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As a member of the TM, Mr. Duracic, did you know in April 1992 that the Territorial Defence of Konjic was organised pursuant to the new regulations on defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know to whom your municipal staff was subordinate at that point?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Konjic, due to the absence of the district headquarters in Mostar, because it was occupied by the Serb Montenegrin aggressors, was subordinate exclusively to the republican TO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, I will not ask you any more questions in this area. This area has been covered by the testimony of other witnesses. And I'm also not going to ask you any questions regarding the situation at Konjic, and your particular work on the strategic defence of it. My question to you is whether you took part in any combat operations in April and May, in and around Konjic; in other words, when was it that you took part in combat operations in Konjic area as a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: My first participation in the combat operations was in May, when the barracks at Ljuta was liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As a participant of this operation in which -- when the Ljuta barracks was taken over, can you tell us whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic did take part in this operation in which the Ljuta barracks was taken over?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. Zejnil Delalic was at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that at that time he was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, was -- were there any changes in the month of May in your municipal staff? And when I say this, I mean were there any substitutions and were any new commanders appointed?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rejgevocic (phoen) was replaced. Mr. Esad Ramic was appointed commander of the Territorial Defence headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, the court also knows what the structure of the defence forces in Konjic was. What I would like to know is whether you know, from your personal experience and knowledge, what efforts were made to place both the TO and the HVO under a unified command which would lead all these activities?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: In April and May both members of the TO and the HVO, at least based on the knowledge that I had, both had the same goals, or shared the same goals, which was the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know if in these joint efforts, joint defence, anyone from the republican headquarters of the Territorial Defence came to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. At that time, and this was right around the time when the new commander was appointed, a member of the republican staff came to visit, and this was Mr. Asim Dzambasovic. He stayed in Konjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Another of your witnesses, isn't it? Why should he say what he is coming to say? That witness is coming, so there is no point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am not going to pursue this line of questioning. But from all this testimony of different citizens of Konjic, you realise that we are laying the foundation for calling Mr. Dzambasovic. I only wanted to link up Mr. Duracic's acquaintance with Mr. Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Call him what you've called him to say. What he can testify to, let him say that. When Asim comes, he should say what he is called upon to testify to. Now you expect him to testify about the Arab journalist, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he also will testify to some other activities of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, in that period of time, which is relevant for Mr. Delalic's defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him go ahead and say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, can you tell me whether during sometime in May of 1992 you became a member of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Could you tell us when this was and to what position you were appointed?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this was in the latter half of May, sometime around 17th or 18th of May, after a meeting of the military top (sic) and the war Presidency. I was not present at the meeting in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: But I did attend the meeting in the afternoon, when the joint command staff was established from members of the TO and the HVO. I was appointed to the position of the chief of engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit number D145(5/10), and the reference number is 7009 to 7011. Mr. Duracic, will you please place the English translation of this text on the ELMO and please review the Bosnian version of the same document. Mr. Duracic, do you recognise this chart?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: This is the organisation chart of the joint command, and here it also gives the Croatian word for it, which is Istosha (phoen), but it's the organisational chart of the joint command of the defence forces of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please point to your position, that is to the duties to which you were appointed? There is a pointer, which you may want to use to show it on the English version on the chart. Thank you, sir. This sufficient, Mr. Duracic. The chart can be returned. It has already been introduced as a Defence Exhibit. Mr. Duracic, did you know Mr. Zejnil Delalic before the war?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him from the 1980's on through 1992. We were acquaintances, I knew Zejnil casually, but I was not part of his circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, did you meet Mr. Zejnil Delalic during the initial stages of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and when did this first meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The first meeting between myself and Mr. Zejnil Delalic, at the beginning of the war, took place when I was tasked by the municipal TO staff to work on the -- on securing the war presidency facility in terms of engineering works. I was told that the war presidency, but all the logistical support, that means sand bags, construction material, cement blocks, et cetera, that for all that material I needed to go to Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that you were -- that you attended a meeting on the 17th or 18th of May, when you were appointed the chief of engineers. Can you tell me whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. By no means. Because -- I'm sorry. I believe that at that time he was still in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Based on what you knew then, did Mr. -- was Mr. Delalic appointed at that time, or at any subsequent time, to any duty in either the municipal staff or the joint command?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The answer to this question is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As a member of staff, did you learn at some point in May, or thereabouts, that Mr. Delalic was tasked with something by the war Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was tasked to use his channels in Zagreb to acquire some equipment and, if possible, weapons for the joint command, and for the units belonging to this joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, do you know that at some point Mr. Zejnil Delalic was appointed coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It was the war Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, was Zejnil Delalic's coordinator ever superior officer to you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Zejnil Delalic was a civilian and I was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since, as you said, you were involved in joint tasks, can you tell me whether Mr. Delalic, as coordinator, had some officials or other persons who were subordinate to him?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he did have -- the position of coordinator is a position of an individual who works as a go-between between two different structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, as a soldier or member of the joint staff, did you ever receive any order from Mr. Delalic's coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: My apologies to you, Mr. Duracic, for asking you a hypothetical question, but had you received an order signed by a coordinator, would this order be obligating to you, or binding to you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: If it were only -- if it was only signed by a coordinator, it would not be a binding order for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: At that time who could issue orders to you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: At that time only the commander of the municipal TO or the commander of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Another potentially hypothetical question. If the signatures of commanders, there was also a signature of the coordinator on one of these documents, would that -- would you interpret that as a document issued by the coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, as a soldier and member of the staff, did you know whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic as coordinator was in a position to appoint anyone?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, do you know a person named Jerko Kostic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Jerko Kostic was appointed assistant commander for security, replacing the former assistant commander for security, Mr. Goran Lokas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, who in the joint command or in any other position was able to appoint persons of a Croatian ethnic background at that time, according to the knowledge that you have?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The persons of Croatian ethnic background could only be appointed to the joint command by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Although this answer may exclude the necessity for my following question, but, nevertheless, in your personal knowledge, do you know whether Mr. Delalic ever appointed Kostic at any function?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have said recently that Delalic is a civilian and a civilian cannot appoint military functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: As a staff member, you probably know that under the order of the commander, there was an unit founded, which was supposed to be subordinated to TG-1, could you tell me, Mr. Duraric, whether Mr. Delalic was tasked concerning this particular unit?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me which unit we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know that in June, one unit from Konjic left for the area of Pazaric and was subordinated to TG-1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is an unit under the name of Gajret.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me, did somebody have certain tasks and obligations for quipping that unit?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that since this is one of the obligations of the war Presidency, they tasked Zejnil Delalic to equip the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were you present when the unit left and whether the headquarters -- was any mention how the send off of the units should be done?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was present. And at the headquarters, it was arranged that Mr. Delalic be given the honour to greet or to send off the unit because this was the first equipped unit we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since you were present at the send off and you also know for the arrangement, the headquarters, can you tell me, Mr. Duraric, whether during this send off relating to the Gajret unit, did Mr. Delalic have any command authority over it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, I will ask you something on another topic. The tribunal has sufficient data that the municipal staff planned and conducted the operation directed toward Boracko Lake, under the name of Oganj. And that prior to the operation, the HVO gave up its taking part. Did you personally take part in the preparation in the planning of the operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Not only me, but the entire joint command. All the branches of the armed forces, the head of the headquarters and brigade commanders, they all took part in the planning of that action, which was directed toward liberating of our occupied territories. And Boracko Jezero UCA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, can you tell me whether Mr. Delalic took part together with you in the joint command in the planning of this particular combat operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, because at that time he was still a civilian.
