utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: After the commencement of the operation, who was in charge of it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The commander was. The commander of joint command, Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Duraric, take part, direct participation in the operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was your function and what was your location, where were you during the combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Vranske Stijene. This is where we had one of the centres for communications for the Oganj Operation. The station was under the number Oganj 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I was warned that the transcript may have been -- there may have been an error in the transcript. You said the commander of the operation was a commander of the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, commander of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tell me now, since you were Vranske Stijene during the operation, how long did the operation take?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It lasted a little bit over one month. And the number of units for performing of tactical tasks remained there longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: During all that time at Vranske Stijene was there Mr. Delalic with you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me please, Mr. Duraric, what were your tasks, what jobs were yours at Vranske Stijene?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I was there as the head of the engineering services and my task was to give security and engineering to secure the directions of the attack. And since this is an area between Bridiko (translation interrupted) and it's a mountainous region, I had to break through for certain links to establish the roads because until then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on). It's not his task.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But I would like to know, since you were at the same place, what were Delalic's tasks?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, since he had a two month experience by then concerning logistical support and so his only task was to transfer requests from units towards the municipal headquarters towards -- through communication links concerning logistical support and security of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since you said that this was also a communication centre, Oganj 1, one of the centres, did you and Mr. Delalic report to that centre? Did you use it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think the transcript is again wrong. I said you should ask about the task of Zejnil Delalic and not his task. I don't know, what does it mean? There are so many mistakes about the remarks that I make. I am very sorry about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise because I cannot follow the transcript at the same time. But my first question referred to functions of Mr. Duraric and the second one for Mr. Delalic. I believe this was also interpreted in the manner and the responses were according to that. It is impossible for me and for my colleague who does not understand our language to follow. We will speak slowly so that interpreters could interpret because such situations were not in the best of interest of the court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It must have been interpreted wrongly. The first question was, what were my functions at Vranske Stijene?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And you then described your engineering services, is it true?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The second question posed to you referred to tasks of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I also described that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Duraric, since you were together with Mr. Delalic for a month at the same spot, was there at any moment, Mr. Delalic your commander? Was he in command over you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I have already said that. He was drafted just recently. He was an ordinary soldier and I was already the head of the engineering staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In addition to you, who was also at that spot at Vranske Stijene?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: During the first days of the operation, in addition to me and Mr. Delalic, we had the commander of joint command, although by that time the HVO gave up participation, then the head of the headquarters, Mr. Cerovac. At that time, he was assistant commander for operative tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Don't concentrate on Mr. Delalic at all. I thought he's your client.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Honourable Chamber, I will repeat the question concerning tasks of Mr. Delalic if it was misinterpreted. The witness did answer. Please tell me what tasks at Vranske Stijene during that one month on the conduct of the operation did Mr. Delalic have?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: During the operation at Vranske Stijene, and not at Vranske Stijene, but during the operation, Zejnil Delalic had the task that upon a request of units who participated in combat operations, if they need equipment, they would request that from him because it could not -- they could not communicate directly with the main centre in Konjic, so he transferred those requests to Mr. Catic or Tahirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again, because of the transcript errors, did at any moment of the Operation Borci, Mr. Delalic was in charge to you personally or any other soldiers who took part in the operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, would you also tell me whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic, concerning the tasks he performed, was he able to give out orders to the engineering services to the artillery or some other type units which participated in the operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many times I need to repeat. I have said several times, Zejnil Delalic could not give out orders to nobody in the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (Microphone not on). Not less than four times here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I believe this wasn't clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since you were at Vranske Stijene during the entire period, at the place where you were situated, were there certain visits from Konjic or from other some other places?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: At the area of Vranske Stijene, since the operation took longer, longer period of time, and the commander and commander in chief, Mr. Cerovac, had to see the units, they would return in a day or two and I remember that once the President of the war Presidency himself came. I don't remember anybody else's visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, do you remember that at any period were there foreigners in that area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I believe they introduced themselves as being journalists from some Arab countries. I do not remember exactly which country, was in question. There was a cameraman, a journalist and a translator.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Duraric, were you personally present to the conversation that journalist had with Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell us in brief what they talked about?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: They were mainly interested in why the war began and then Delalic explained that there was an aggression in Bosnia-Herzegovina and that the people -- there was an uprising among the people to defend themselves. Then he also spoke about poor equipment of our soldiers. They were poorly equipped with arms and supplies. Then he spoke about how western countries still do not realise that this was an aggression directed towards us and that the Arab countries get very little help.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, please tell me whether during your conversation with the journalist, did anybody of the present introduce Mr. Delalic as a commander?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, by all means (sic).

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How were you introduced to each other then?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Just by our names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since the chamber saw a few shots from the area, a few excerpts, can you to tell me whether at that region, were there any notices or signs written in a foreign language?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. I believe that you and the Chamber will understand that the lessons were participants in the war, people of 18, 19, 20, up to 22 years of age. And to prove to themselves how big they are, they would write such signs, such as pentagon, NATO and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was there anywhere a sign saying, "The Main Regional Commander"?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. At least I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Duraric, did in Konjic exist at all the commander of our region at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, it never did and it still does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, did those soldiers maybe write a sign that would mention in office?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have said everything. I believe the sign said what I already said. It was under a tent which could contain until two soldiers. And I believe my older son, and another soldier under the name of Irfan wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would now ask to show the tape 2, just a brief excerpt from Vranske Stijene to see whether the witness knows the shots. It is only about a second or two. Tape 1. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Were you able to see, Mr. Duraric?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, the monitor doesn't show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Would you please rewind the tape and you press the first button stating "Video Monitor." Could you play it now, please. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the sign at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Continue please. Can the camera go up? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is tape used as Prosecutor's evidence, Number 146. Do you, Mr. Duraric, can you claim in full face that this is the only sign that was created in the way that you mentioned and found in the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I fully acknowledge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you whether during the operation, at a given time, was there a change in the command post of the operation?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Esad Ramic was injured and he took over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I would now ask you, Mr. Duraric, something connected to a new topic. You, as Konjic person, know of the blockade of the road in Bradina and the combat operations directed to it, can you tell me whether you personally had ever any contact with the barracks and the detention facility in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the barracks, but never with the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When and how many times did you visit the barracks in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: When I gave my solemn statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Although you were not personally connected to the prison, did you know that the army barracks also contained one?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Almost everybody in Konjic knew that there are detainees in Celebici and members of SDS. We captured those people when we liberated Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Duraric, ever find out about mistreatment of those prisoners or an abuse of them?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Although, my younger son during the first days had a post in the prison. He never mentioned any mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, tell me something about something else I wanted to ask you. Did you at a certain moment find out that Mr. Delalic was appointed as a military commander?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were at Vranske Stijene together when, through communication links, from the headquarters in Konjic, he learned that he was appointed commander of TG-1. For all of us it was great honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell the chamber when this happened exactly? When you found out at Vranske Stijene through your communication links that Mr. Delalic was appointed to the post?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It could have been around the end of July. I do not remember exactly, but between the 27th and the 29th, I am pretty sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I have a hypothetical question, Mr. Duraric. Would it have been possible that Mr. Delalic, appointed to this function earlier without his knowledge, without it being communicated to him and without you knowing about it at Vranske Stijene?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It was impossible not to know if such an order came to the headquarters or the joint command in Konjic. That same moment it had to be communicated to the position where Mr. Delalic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duraric, can you claim that Mr. Delalic was at Vranske Stijene until the end of July until the moment he learned of the order of the notification?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your honourable chamber, is it time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on.)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: About another ten questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's likely to testify to. And you must have covered them all by now. Plus ten more irrelevant questions. The Trial Chamber will now rise and we'll come back at 2.30 p.m.. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.02 p.m. 23 24 25 --- Upon resuming at 2.30 p.m. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I ask the court to excuse Ms. Boler for the rest of the afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, you will recall that before the break we left off when you testified that in late July, between 27 and 29, you learned that Mr. Delalic was appointed to the commander of the Tactical Group 1. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, can you please tell me whether at that time you became a superior officer to Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Delalic at that point become a superior officer in charge of the municipal headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Commander of the Tactical Group has command and control only of the units which were -- which he was given to carry out the particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, did you at any time during the period while Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, yourself a member of the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And did you, during the period of time when Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were a soldier of the Tactical Group 1 and subordinate to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, I am going to ask you another hypothetical question. Had you, as a member of the joint command of municipal staff of TO Konjic receive an order from Mr. Delalic's commander of Tactical Group 1, would this order have been a binding one for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said that he was not subordinate. My additional question to him was whether he would still carry out an order which he might have received from commander of Tactical Group. However, if this -- if you believe that this is implied in his answer that he could not carry out an order from a person who was not his commander, then I am satisfied. However, I am giving the witness an additional option to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. In no way. It is only my immediate commander who is -- whose orders were binding to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Duracic, just a very brief area of questioning. You testified before this Tribunal that Mr. Delalic provided significant logistical support of the Territorial Defence and the defence forces of Konjic. As a citizen of Konjic, do you know whether other citizens of Konjic also provided assistance to the defence forces of -- in as much as they could?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. All citizens of Konjic who had any financial means did provide assistance, and they provided their financial and other support in provision of the necessary material, and Mr. Zejnil Delalic was certainly one of them. I only want to point out that as a business person who had spent a fair amount of time in the west, he was much better connected, and he was able to -- much easier provide materials and equipment that we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Duracic. This is enough in a way of an answer to the question that I asked. As a member of the defence forces in Konjic, do you know whether in 1992 certain formations, like Green Berets or Patriotic League, or other organised groups, were active in the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I emphatically stated, with the exception of the HVO, the Army, and the MUP, there were no other armed formations in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You spent one month in Vranske Stijene in the rugged terrain with Mr. Delalic, and you worked in the field with him in 1992. Can you tell me whether you ever heard or personally see that Mr. Delalic had any responsibility or authority over the Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I had no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: On the basis of your personal knowledge of these events, did you know whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic has any kind of control over the staff in the prison or the authority to punish these persons?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. As I stated previously, I had no connection with the prison. It was not part of my responsibilities, so I was not in a position to know whether Mr. Delalic had any authority there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And while you were together at the Vranske Stijene, did you ever notice that Mr. Delalic had any contact or connection with either the staff or the prison in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I emphasise no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Duracic. This concludes my questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? CROSS-EXAMINED BY MR. OLUJIK:

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. May it please the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Duracic, I am Mr. Olujic, I am defence counsel for Zdravko Mucic. I would like to ask several questions. I will be brief. I just want to restate what my learned colleague has already said, that we need to take into account the needs for interpreting, and I just want to recall that warning.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, during your examination-in-chief, while my colleague, Ms. Residovic, questioned you, you mentioned names of Mr. Lokas and Mr. Kostic as persons who were in that -- in this investigative commission. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not what I said. What I stated was that Mr. Goran Lokas was assistant commander for security in the municipal staff, and after his traffic accident he was replaced by Mr. Kostic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me, Mr. Duracic, whether Mr. Lokas was in charge of security? Would it be correct to say that Mr. Lokas was under the authority of the public security station?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. It is possible that he had been previously, but when he became member of the joint command, he was under the authority of the commander of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And could you please tell me where Mr. Kostic used to work previously?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know where he worked previously, but I only know that he came from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: However, you do not know where he worked?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could we say that in the spring and summer of 1992, due to different circumstances, the population of the Konjic municipality was inadequately armed and organised?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, could we say that the population was not sufficiently armed and organised to counter what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: We certainly could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Very well. Would you agree that after the fall of Bradina, which you mentioned, there were still gangs of Chetniks roaming around the woods?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, could we also agree that there were other renegades and bandits around?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What I mean is not just the Chetniks, but others as well who roamed around and they were armed and a threat to law and peace, law and order?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIK
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, this concludes my examination. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Judge Jan noticed certain misinterpretation. We have just seen a misinterpretation which is completely opposite of what the question that I asked was. On page 68, line 10 it states whether I had asked whether Mr. Duracic was a superior officer to Mr. Delalic. My question was whether Mr. Zejnil Delalic had became a superior officer to Mr. Duracic after he had become the commander of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So can we please have the transcript corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, defence counsel of Hazim Delic has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May it please the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed. Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, like Mr. Moran, very few. EXAMINED BY MS. MCMURREY:

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Duracic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I am Ms. McMurrey and I represent Mr. Esad Landzo. From your testimony to my colleague, Ms. Residovic, I believe you stated that immediately upon the call for mobilisation you joined the Territorial Defence. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He didn't mention the call, but he said immediately he joined.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I guess it was my interpretation of it. If you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But you did join immediately?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And, in fact, when you joined, your two sons joined along with you, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, you knew Mr. Esad Landzo as he was growing up, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In fact, you and your family not only lived on the same street of 15th of September Street, but you lived in the same apartment building, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same stairwell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And one of your sons was about the same age as Mr. Landzo, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the younger son, the late one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In fact, when you say the late son, that son was killed in an automobile accident in 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: But your son was a friend of Mr. Landzo's while they were growing up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, do you remember Mr. Landzo as a boy?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true to say that he was a kind of withdrawn young man?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And another thing about your apartment building. In your apartment building, Serbs, Croats and Muslims all lived in harmony together, until the war broke out, and there wasn't any prejudice among you, was there?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And your late son that grew up with Mr. Landzo, he was one of the young recruits for the Territorial Defence that was transferred to Celebici sometime in the middle of June of 1992; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the first week of June, and he only stayed there for one week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Your son was there for one week; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And your son never mentioned any mistreatment of any prisoners while he was there, did he?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at all, because in all likelihood there wasn't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And all of these young men that were sent to Celebici, they were all 18, 19, 20 years old, with no former military experience; wouldn't that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who was in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, your son and Mr. Landzo, you know for a fact that they had never served in the JNA, they had never served any military duty before, had they?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And my one last question is: If you can remember, your street and your apartment building in Konjic suffered from heavy shelling and several people were killed in front of everybody. Would that be accurate to say?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Duracic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Questions of the Prosecution, please. CROSS-EXAMINED BY MR. NIEMANN:

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said that you had met Mr. Delalic when you were providing -- when you -- I withdraw the question, Your Honour. When you were providing security for the war Presidency, you met Mr. Delalic at that stage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And who gave the orders to provide security at the war Presidency building?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I received the order from the commander of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And you were working with Mr. Delalic on this project, jointly with him?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What exactly were -- what exactly was the relationship between you at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: It was just simple a acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Why wasn't this work carried out by the civil defence, or the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Simply because I was a specialist for the area. I was captain first class in the former army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, you said that Mr. Delalic was sent to Zagreb by the war Presidency. Were you aware that he had also received authority from the Ministry of Defence in Sarajevo in relation to this project?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: What project are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: To acquire arms and equipment in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know that he had received it, because I was in no position to do so. It was not within my authority to know these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, if you were aware that he was authorised by the -- he was authorised by the war Presidency to enter in joint actions of troops at this time, that is in May of 1992, would that alter your opinion as to whether or not he had a military function to perform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please ask the first question. The question is in two parts, that he was ordered to join the joint staff, and then ask the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If -- I don't want to ask the first question, because it doesn't lead to the end result of what I want to do. But I'll ask him whether he was aware of the special authorisation, and perhaps it might be shown to him. Might the witness be shown Exhibit 99-7-4, please. Just look to paragraph 3, if you would for me, please. Now, I take it you haven't seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have not seen this document before either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, it's dated 2nd of May 1992. Looking at paragraph 3, does that paragraph alter your opinion as to whether or not at that stage, in May of 1992, he had any military function to perform?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has not seen the document before. He has already stated his knowledge about the duties of Mr. Delalic at that period and he did it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am asking him to express his opinion after seeing something he hadn't seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It was not an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He expressed an opinion previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You're now asking him whether he was having military responsibility at that time. That's not an opinion. It's a statement of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't mind if it's a fact, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you believe that that changes the facts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He said he doesn't know. (Microphone not on).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question of the Prosecutor at all, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, you said that in May of 1992, Mr. Delalic performed only a civil function. I am asking you to look at this document, which is in May of 1992, and in particular, at paragraph 3. After having read that, I am asking you, do you still say that he only performed a civilian function?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, the witness stated what his knowledge was in 1992 and these are facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: In that document he said what he knew. As far as he knew he performed a civil function.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, having a look at that document, you are wrong when you express that opinion, is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What he said was not an opinion. It was a fact known to him. I don't think he could be reprimanded because he did not know something has happened. That's a different matter. He did not say that it never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you had two states of affairs, Your Honour, one which he believes to be the position and one which is demonstrated by documentary material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He did not know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If he doesn't know about it, then clearly it's a legitimate course of cross-examination to demonstrate that he didn't have these disposed war facts which enabled him to express his views on something. That's what I am seeking to do. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Does that document refer to a military function?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It says, all kinds of agreements on possible joint actions of troops from other areas. Your Honours, perhaps, the document can be shown to you. But I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's moving on. (Microphone not on). So don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, you say that when you were with Mr. Delalic at Vranske Stijene -- I think I have got the pronunciation of that correct -- that he was there until the end of July. Are you saying at no stage he returned to Konjic during the month of July?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have said that Vranske Stijene, being the terrain it is, we had no water, no electrical power, he could only leave in the afternoon and return in the evening to maybe take a bath. But I guarantee he has not done that more than once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Are you aware that while Mr. Delalic was at Vranske Stijene, he signed a release document for Celebici for a prisoner in Celebici, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I was personally present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, had Mr. Cerovac asked you to sign the release document on his behalf, would you have done so?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me, when you're at Vranske Stijene, what was the structure of the command? I believe you had no ranks at that stage. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not have ranks, but we had positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. And Mr. Delalic had a position?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was just an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. So what distinguished an ordinary soldier from a person with a position?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: An appointed person has a responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. But how would the ordinary foot soldier come to know that? You don't carry your authorisation around with you all the time, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I do not understand, who wouldn't know?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How would the ordinary foot soldier know that you're the person in command and authority and you had no ranks, you only had positions, how did they differentiate between people with no command and people with authority?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Each commander of a basic unit knew who is his commander and who are the personnel within the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What's a basic unit, tell me about this, what is it? How many people are in it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The lowest unit was a squad, nine fighters, plus a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And what squad was Mr. Delalic in?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: We did not have squads when it comes to him. He was a part of our communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, who was his immediate commander, if he was just an ordinary foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Both his and my commander was Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, if he was in charge of communications, isn't that a position?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, since it was a communication station to connect to other station, the main centre for communication was in Konjic where the head of communications was Mr. Sultanic Arif.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So at this particular time, it's a fact, isn't it, the soldiers wouldn't have known who their commanders were, wouldn't necessarily have known who their commanders were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remember, Sultanic has been here, one of the witnesses for the Defence has been here, has been in charge of the communications unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Sultanic, Mr. Delalic's commander, was he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only for that particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So Mr. Sultanic was there giving orders to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No audible answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What about knowing about who was in command of other units? How would soldiers know who was in charge of other units or had authority over them, apart from their own?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness has already responded that each soldier knew who his commander was, and all the commanders knew who the staff members of the headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, if Madam Residovic cares to read the transcript, she will know that I asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Which is, how did the soldiers know who the commanders of other units were?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: You do not necessarily have to know who the commanders of other units were. He only needs to know who his immediate commander is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You mentioned the visit to the mountain by the Arab journalists, who brought them up to the place where you and Mr. Delalic were at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: They were brought by our courier. Before that they visited the office of the commander and our positions of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You would agree with me, wouldn't you, that it was considered in your best interest to assist these journalists and to provide them with information, so that could in turn be transmitted to the international community?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: In any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Why did they introduce the Arab journalists from overseas, who had come here especially to conduct this interview to an ordinary foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of why they were brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of why the person that was to speak on behalf of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that location happened to be an ordinary foot soldier?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether this foot soldier was to speak for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that was the choice most likely made by the reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So, is it the customary practice of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is it, to have ordinary foot soldiers speak on their behalf to foreign journalists?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Until they were forbidden to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, didn't you say that during the Oganj Operation, military operation, operation fire, I think it's known as, Mr. Delalic had a logistics problem, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You'd agree with me that the provision of logistics, especially in the field in the face of battle is a military function?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but only during combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, how did you know that the war Presidency appointed Mr. Delalic as a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I knew because I was a member of staff of the joint command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I didn't know that this was in issue at all, his appointment as a coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Do you know of anybody else who, or have you ever heard of anybody else being appointed to the role of coordinator in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is not a question at issue and it did not refer to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am asking if he knew someone in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who was appointed to the role of coordinator at that time. It's a simple yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have to tell me who should he coordinate with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Naturally Dr. Dzambajovic clearly stated it wasn't uncommon to appoint such a person as coordinator. It wasn't new. So I don't see what this gentleman would say again. Because that was the function of who appointed Delalic as coordinator. He didn't find it strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, who provided the necessary engineering support for Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the Operation Borci?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: TG-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: TG-1 was with regard to the lifting off the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who supplied engineering support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness to see Exhibit 193. I have copies, Your Honour, of the exhibit. Have you ever seen that before?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And your name appears there, does it not, as the head of engineering?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If you'd received a copy of this order, would you have obeyed it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: There's no signature by my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I see. Well, how do you know that isn't an order that had been sent to you on behalf of your commander?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness said he has never seen the document and to my question that his answer was he was never a member of command of a tactical group. I do not see the point in these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: How would you know that it hadn't been sent out on behalf of your commander?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. I repeat the objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't see how it concerns him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It's his name, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. He said it wasn't signed by his commander. He said as long as it wasn't signed by his commander, he would not have obeyed it. That's what he said. You're now asking whether it was signed on behalf of his commander, unknown to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: If it hadn't been signed on behalf of your commander, you wouldn't have known that, would you?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Well, I am asking you, you say that you definitely wouldn't obey this order if you had received it. Now my next question to you is, but how would you know that it hadn't been sent out on behalf of the supreme command in Sarajevo, which was ultimately your commander, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat the objection because this is an inauthentic document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He can answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I would have known because the preamble states, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the army of B and H Tactical Group 1, and instead of TG-1, it should have said, municipal staff, municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence or the joint command for Konjic. There should have been full name of the commander underneath, together with his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now you said in part of your evidence that you -- that some of the people that you captured when you liberated Bradina were sent to Celebici, do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have not said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What did you say? Perhaps, I have got the transcript incorrectly noted in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I said that when we liberated Bradina, they captured and the entire Town of Konjic knew that these captured people were taken to the barracks in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Who took them to the barracks in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You mentioned that your son was in Celebici for a week, he was in the Territorial Defence, was he, when he went to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure whether he was in a member of the Territorial Defence. I think he was a reserve for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Now, I think you had mentioned at one stage that the President of the war Presidency came to the theatre of operations, military operations, when you and Mr. Delalic were there together, do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I do remember, but he was not within the zone of combat operations, but he came to the communications centre of Oganj 1 Operation at Vranske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did he converse with both you and Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: And what was he doing there, just inspecting or what?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The war Presidency has its obligation to support and supply their units, so he came to see what our needs were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The war Presidency at a local level is also responsible for the political direction of operations in order to protect the municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No. This is solely under the authority of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So are you suggesting that the municipality and the war Presidency has no interest in the preservation and protection of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You don't appreciate this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had the President of the war Presidency, it should have been clarified then (sic).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you answer my question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that this was not an obligation of the war Presidency, but their obligation is to support and supply the units which perform tasks of defence of the territorial municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you attend meetings of the war Presidency or attend meetings where members of the war Presidency were present?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you ever have the task of providing information to the war Presidency --

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I'll just show you a document, if I may. And I have a copy for Your Honours. Just looking the at the second paragraph of that document, if you would, is what I am mainly interested in.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: I have never seen this document and I wouldn't wish to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I just want to know from you whether the reference in the second paragraph is a reference to the chief of engineers services, whether that's a reference to you? Says, "Introduction by Chief of Engineers Service". And it may not be, I am just asking if it relates to you.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: If this were referred to me, it is most likely that I would have received this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You don't remember seeing it though?

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Did you understand my question? My question simply was, the reference there in paragraph number 2, "The Chief of Engineer Service," is that a reference to your title and position or was there some other position occupied by somebody else who was called "Chief of Engineer Service"? That is really my question.

utterances.speaker: MUSTAFA DZELILOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal staff and the joint command that would be me. But, I repeat, had this paper referred to me, I would have received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think you are discharged. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have the next witness. I will call him. However, I need to let you know that I personally do not feel quite well today and if I am unable to continue with full concentration, I will let you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have a co-counsel, who can carry on, on your behalf.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you are aware of the fact that one counsel is engaged in preparation of a single witness. I will do my utmost and I ask for you understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Incidentally before you start, I see in the next list of witnesses you filed, you're indicating that at some time your witnesses 1 through 7 are able to travel to The Hague between the 2nd of June and the 12th. That your witnesses 8 through 14 are able to travel, to testify, the week 22nd to 26th. Is that what you really intend to do? You know that you cannot do that. I indicated to you before we went on, for this holiday, one day holiday, that you have to supplement your number of witnesses to ensure that we take all of them. You now remember that I said that? Now, you think you can stall the progress of the Trial Chamber by refusing to bring your witnesses. This is what you intend to do. Well, you will have to get updated and let them be here because we'll carry on until your witnesses are exhausted. The Trial Chamber will continue sitting. We will not, for any reason, have a break for that purpose. If you are unable to complete, you have to close your case. Call your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will ask you that -- to hear me out before this testimony. We have done whatever we could, however, these witnesses have their professional obligations. We have talked to their managers, we have talked to some other people who are in the United States. They had expected to be here at another time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please call all your witnesses. We'll examine them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: EXAMINED BY MS. RESIDOVIC:

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Will you please introduce yourself to the court by stating your full first and last names.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I am Asim Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, before I proceed to ask you questions which I have prepared, I need to draw your attention to a technical point. We both speak the same language and you would be able to very quickly and easily respond to all of my questions. However, it is very important that each question and answer is heard by the Trial Chamber and everybody else present here in the courtroom. Given this fact, will you please, when I ask you a question, you wait until it is being interpreted, and you will be able to hear the interpretation coming through a headset on the desk next to you, and only then answer the question. Did you understand what I just told you, Mr. Dzambasovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I fully understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Your welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, can you tell me where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on 27 June 1949 in Rogatica in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was your formal education and when you acquired it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I completed my elementary school in Rogatica, teachers college in Sarajevo, military academy in Belgrade, and superior military academy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So what is your profession, Mr. Dzambasovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I am a professional officer by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, can you tell the court what is your rank today in the Army of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Federation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I have the rank of a brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Brigadier. Where were you on 6 April 1992, when the war in Herzegovina, Bosnia-Herzegovina broke out?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: On 6 April 1992, I was with the Yugoslav People's Army and I was specifically at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What was your specific position in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: My specific duty at the time was chief of staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: What was your rank in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I was Lieutenant-Colonel in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Brigadier. Did there come a time in 1992 when you became involved in the defence forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I became involved. On 13 April 1992, I reported to the republican staff of the TO Bosnia-Herzegovina, and from then on I have been in the units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The court has already heard enough about the armed forces at the disposal of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time of the outbreak of war. My question to you is at the time when you reported to the republican staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did Bosnia have this armed force at the time when it was attacked?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, both in Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the time of the attack and aggression, did not have an organised armed force, and it took steps to organise it as soon as it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The court has already heard a number of facts and witnesses relating to the arming of the Serb people. Since you were a soldier, an officer of the former JNA, until April 6th, 1992, could you tell us, from your own experience, whether the JNA did arm Serb population and the SDS political party?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is the position of the Prosecution to examine Calic. Why do you want to go to that question again?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After Dr. Calic, the Prosecution called another witness to testify to the same facts, and I believe that these are actual fact witnesses as opposed to the witnesses who were only -- who only testified on the basis of documents. I was under the impression that the court prefers witnesses who are direct witnesses to the facts. However, if this is sufficient for Your Honours, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: there is again a mistake in the transcript. I said when they examined Dr. Calic, not Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is another a mistake in the transcript. I said when the Prosecution examined Dr. Calic, not examined Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you see, Your Honours, we are facing different types of problems. You see, it just gives us an additional need for us to review transcripts, which is an additional burden to us, but we are grateful for you for pointing out mistakes in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mistakes happen here repeatedly by so many witnesses. I think it doesn't improve on what they have said. We've heard that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Brigadier, you said that you reported to the republican staff on the 13th of April. Could you tell us now, from your own personal experience, whether the state bodies did respond immediately by adopting regulations that would provide for establishment of a defence force?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As early as 8 April, as the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and was internationally recognised. The state bodies did indeed take emergency steps in order to adopt certain regulations and legislation which would regulate the system of defence as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, in light of this fact, and this fact is already known to the court, did you, in carrying out these new tasks of the republican staff and the Ministry of Defence, at some point in the spring of 1992 did you visit Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after the new legislation was passed on the 14th, 14th of April that is, I received an order to go as a military expert into the territory of Konjic municipality in order to organise and assist the Territorial Defence in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Why did the republican staff decide that it was necessary that certain experts within its ranks, such as you, would need to go to the Konjic area? Did the Konjic area have a particular significance for defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, among others. There were some other areas as well in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Konjic was one of the more significant ones. It has a significant military industry. It has significant military facilities, which were used in the system of control and command and the communication systems. It had significant depots, warehousing facilities, and some less significant facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Dzambasovic. Can you tell us how you personally arrived in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was very difficult. Even though the distance between Sarajevo and Konjic is about 45 minute drive in a car, it took me about three days to reach it; that is, on the road, Sarajevo, Tarcin, Konjic, the SDS extremists had erected barricades at Ivan Sjedlo Pass so that I could not use that road to get to Konjic. After that, on the suggestion of my staff, I opted for a different -- Kresevo, Tojnica, Dusina and Buturovic Polje Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. When you reached Konjic, when was this; what period, what month -- how specifically can you remember?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: This was the latter half of May -- of April, 18th or 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived in Konjic, did you at that time know the military and civilian leadership of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know anyone, and this was an additional difficulty for me. I didn't even know any people there. I didn't have friends, nor did I go there officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: When you came to Konjic, you probably met these leaderships. Could you tell me who was the commander of the municipal staff at the time of your visit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Commander of the municipal staff was also an officer. He was a captain first class, Enver Rezdepagic, who had been appointed after the new legislation on the reorganisation, that is on the organisation of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, how long did you stay in Konjic, until when?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed in Konjic until approximately 21st, 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, can you tell us what were your priority tasks which you were supposed to carry out in the territory of this municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: My priority tasks were to assist the local -- the military authorities to set up the Territorial Defence in the Konjic area, and given that this was the initial period and that in Bosnia-Herzegovina we did not have enough professional soldiers, that is officers, there was an urgent need to set up a popular armed resistance as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, can you now tell us what specific steps were taken in the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence while you were present there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: The organisation of this task is a very complex one. We had conditions which were far worse than the normal conditions under which you normally would prepare for a military exercise. This was the reality that we were facing, and a list of activities in which we engaged in was a very long one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, among these -- on this long list of activities while you were down there in the -- was the general mobilisation called in the territory of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the decree with the force of law, which was adopted sometime after 8 April, and certain instructions which we received, the general mobilisation was also called in that area, as it was called in all the other areas, and a number of problems arose in that connection, especially the citizens of Serb ethnic background constructed (sic) this mobilisation in different ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please refer to questions which have a bearing on the role of Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, please tell me whether during this period you met Mr. Zejnil Delalic in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met him on the premises of the public security station and the municipal TO headquarters. In fact, we may not have met at all, but I was told that he was a very interesting personality, that he was one of the outstanding business people in Bosnia-Herzegovina that would be able to engage in logistics, and that in that respect he is probably the most qualified and the most able.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You said that you met him for the first time in the TO and the MUP building. When you met him, was he a member of the TO or of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not. Not at all. At that time in this period, while I was visiting down there, since I had insight into the full structure and organisation, I know that he did not have such role.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, did you meet Mr. Zejnil Delalic again in April, and if you did, when was it, on what occasion it was, and what did he do at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: We met on several other occasions, and this was precisely in this initial period, at the entrance to the city or to the town of Konjic where his house was located, and our contacts were social ones, that we would meet to go to have coffee together. And he was a very sociable person anyway. And since I had come to an area which was completely unknown to me, he was an interesting person to know and to talk to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, when you arrived in Konjic, did you learn from the municipal staff, or other competent authorities, anything about the take-over of some military facilities in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was something that I was interested in, and, in conversation with the commander of the TO staff, I learned that facilities near Celebici were military facilities, that they were taken over in a peaceful manner, which I was glad about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we will now rise and we'll reassemble at 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Judge Jan raised the other day, that an issue about Exhibit 99, P-99 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: All formations or the other. We've had a certification of it, Your Honours, and the translations section say the correct translation is all formations. I have a copy with a certification on it, which I would ask be attached to the exhibit. Perhaps it might be shown to Madam Residovic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, upon your suggestion, we have gone through the document which is the Prosecutor's evidence 99 and the expert's report and we noticed a difference. Both documents, from what we can see, have been put together by the service of this Tribunal and there is a significant and important difference, so we wanted to forward a letter to the interpreter service to determine upon the correct translation. What we could see, according to the English translations, all the -- all that was translated as formation or composition, but never as an unit. So we find it best for the interpreter service to go through both documents and have a written statement on the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Because it makes a lot of difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We've had that done and that's the response. Your Honours will see when you look at the document, that it's been so certified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The two translations make a lot of difference in the sense of how you understand it. Is it units? Is it formations? That's why I got your attention to this difference, so that it can be sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's what we've done, Your Honour. The one I have just showed to Madam Residovic, I didn't intend that she keep it, but that she see it, would be attached to the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We agree because I can see that there is a verification of the interpreters service, so, therefore, this is an official translation of the document. It seems to me in the transcript, it was translated all the time as "all formation". So I would request that this document be a part of the evidence of 245/6-51 A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we continue with your witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Prior to the break, Mr. Dzambasovic, you have said to us that you were given an information about the take-over of the Celebici barracks. Do you know, or was it told to you then, who conducted this take-over and in which manner?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I have said I was interested in it and I know that this was done by the unit of the Territorial Defence and the police unit, the MUP unit, in a way without combat through peaceful means and I was very glad about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, have you learned then whether Mr. Delalic played any role in the take-over of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I really do not know anything about that. From the military point of view, I don't know how he could have a role. And I believe that in that part he played no role whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: So you did not have that information at the time. Mr. Dzambasovic, you came from the republican staff of the Territorial Defence and the ministry which were, at that time, the supreme command of the army in formation. Have you had any knowledge about legal authorities of the newly formed country demanded for military facilities at the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina be put under control of legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was quite normal. A Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not have military facilities, nor the arms, nor the equipment. And we tried to put those objects under our control and into function. This was our interest, our goal as well as a goal of all those who fought for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Dzambasovic, after you have learned of the take-over of the Celebici barracks, did you, yourself, visit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: I visited the barracks on several occasions, as well as other facilities in that area. For the first time I was accompanied by the commander, Rezdepagic, simply so that I could see the entire situation and to, in a way, suggest or council what needs to be done to establish a defence system.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: The chamber already knows that the Celebici barracks used to be storage of the JNA. Would you tell us, please, whether the facilities as you have seen it during the take-over was prepared to accommodate a large number of people? Could it be used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: Those facilities were constructed with a particular purpose, to store fuels and lubricants, with several facilities underground. And I believe there were two or three buildings with three or four offices, so there were no further facilities to accommodate units or people. This was mainly storage space.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: You visited the facility with the then commander of the municipal staff, Captain Enver Rezdepagic. Tell me whether you knew who appointed Mr. Rezdepagic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: It was known to me, I was interested in it. As soon as the documents arrived, as soon as they were put into force, the war Presidency and the municipal staff wanted to put into practice as soon as possible the new regulations, and they suggested the new commander. And in the period of my presence, an official appointment came from the republican staff in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: In your knowledge, at the moment, was Mr. Zejnil Delalic, whom you've met at where you've described before, did he have any influence upon the appointment of the commanders of municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: He could not have had an influence. It couldn't have been had by anybody, but anybody could suggest. In this specific case, he could not have had an influence upon the appointment of a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Since you spent almost an entire month in the Konjic area at the initial period of the war, did Mr. Delalic, under your knowledge of his tasks, was he at that time a civilian or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
utterances.text: He was a civilian, and we even envied him for not being able to be civilians at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzambasovic, can you tell me whether the period of your presence in Konjic, did Mr. Delalic leave the area of Konjic, and if you have such knowledge, tell us where he went and for how long he was absent?

utterances.speaker: ASIM DZAMBASOVIC
